hook: Lifespan drugs help heavy male mice most, partly because heavy controls die young.
hook_turn: partly because heavy controls die young.
summary: Across 33,780 mice in the Interventions Testing Program, lifespan benefits in males grew with body weight, from a 6.2% median gain in the lightest quartile to 20.2% in the heaviest. Controls that were heavier died sooner, so part of the gain looks like rescue from obesity-linked risk. The pattern was weak in females, and this is a reanalysis of observational weight data.
title: Body weight modifies the efficacy of lifespan-extending interventions in ad libitum-fed mice
